# UAE E-Invoicing Penalties: Every Fine, What It Could Cost and How to Avoid It

Last updated: [Date] · Reviewed by [Name, UAE tax credential] · Technical review: [Reviewer name, role at Tech&]

UAE e-invoicing penalties are recurring monthly fines, so a late start compounds quickly. This guide gives your finance team four things: every fine in plain English, and a costed exposure for three common scenarios. It also gives you a way to identify your own deadline and a prevention plan with a named owner for each control. Where published sources disagree, we say so and show you which primary text to check.

**Quick answer:** Under Cabinet Decision No. 106 of 2025, the Federal Tax Authority (FTA) can fine businesses that miss their e-invoicing obligations. Failing to implement the Electronic Invoicing System or appoint an Accredited Service Provider costs AED 5,000 per month or part of a month. Each electronic invoice or credit note not issued and transmitted on time costs AED 100, capped at AED 5,000 per month. Voluntary adopters are not penalised.

## What are the UAE e-invoicing penalties under Cabinet Decision No. 106 of 2025?

Cabinet Decision No. 106 of 2025 sets the fines for e-invoicing breaches. Failing to implement the Electronic Invoicing System or appoint an Accredited Service Provider costs AED 5,000 for each month or part of a month. Each invoice or credit note not issued and transmitted on time costs AED 100, capped at AED 5,000 per month.

The Ministry of Finance published the decision in December 2025. It is a [separate Cabinet Decision dedicated to e-invoicing administrative penalties](https://abdelhamidcpa.com/2026/05/29/uae-e-invoicing-system-2026/). It sits under Federal Decree-Law No. 28 of 2022 on Tax Procedures, and the Federal Tax Authority enforces it.

### The six violations at a glance

| Violation (paraphrased from the [MoF decision](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Cabinet-Decision-Violations-and-Penalties-eInvoicing-final-version-en-8.12.25.pdf)) | Plain-English meaning | Example | Who is liable | Fine | Cap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Failure to implement the e-invoicing system, including appointing an ASP, by the deadline | You are not connected through an accredited provider on time | Your mandatory date passes with the ASP contract unsigned | Issuer and recipient | AED 5,000 per month or part month ([source](https://covoro.ai/uae/fta-announces-penalties-for-non-compliance-with-uae-e-invoicing/)) | None stated; recurs monthly ([source](https://kaidolab.com/blog/uae-e-invoicing-asp-deadline-2026/)) |
| Failure to issue and transmit an electronic invoice on time | The invoice is not sent through your ASP in the structured electronic format | A batch of sales invoices goes out as PDFs | Issuer | AED 100 per invoice | AED 5,000 per month ([source](https://www.genzone.com/uae-e-invoicing-2026-guide/)) |
| Failure to issue and transmit an electronic credit note on time | The same rule applied to credit notes | Month-end returns are credited manually | Issuer | AED 100 per credit note | AED 5,000 per month ([source](https://www.genzone.com/uae-e-invoicing-2026-guide/)) |
| Failure to notify the FTA of a system failure within the set period | You must tell the FTA when a fault stops you issuing | An ASP outage goes unreported | Issuer | [Amount per MoF decision] | [Cap per MoF decision] |
| Failure to notify the ASP of changes to your registered data | Your ASP's record of your business must stay current | A new branch is never notified to the ASP | Business in scope | [Amount per MoF decision] | [Cap per MoF decision] |
| Recipient failure to notify the issuer of a system failure | A buyer must tell its supplier when it cannot receive | The buyer's ASP is down and the supplier is not told | Recipient | [Amount per MoF decision] | [Cap per MoF decision] |

Confirm the wording and amounts for rows four to six against the MoF decision before using them in board papers.

These penalties recur. The AED 5,000 applies for each month or part of a month of delay, so one day into a new month counts as a full month. Article 2 excludes voluntary adopters from these penalties.

### Download the penalty summary (PDF)

Enter your email to receive the one-page UAE e-invoicing penalties summary for your board pack: [Download link].

[Image: Infographic summarising the six UAE e-invoicing penalties under Cabinet Decision No. 106 of 2025 with fines in AED]

## When do e-invoicing penalties start, and which phase are you in?

Penalties start only once your mandatory date passes. Voluntary adoption opens from 1 July 2026, and large businesses at or above the [AED 50 million threshold](https://worldcompanysetup.com/en/blog/uae-e-invoicing-mandate-dubai-timeline-penalties/) move first. Once you are mandatory, [AED 5,000 per month plus AED 100 per missing invoice](https://growacross.com/insights/uae-e-invoicing-2026) can apply.

The phases are set by [Ministerial Decisions No. 243 and 244 of 2025](https://qeemahcloud.com/en/blog/uae-e-invoicing-deadlines-2026/?srsltid=AU7gw4WNyQVaepjxnAO0IBhnccG4lwbSJEKQue8sg3o-iwSYmvpmKNG9). Treat the official text as the only authority for your dates.

### Why different sources quote different dates

| Source | AED 50m+ ASP deadline | AED 50m+ go-live | Everyone else |
|---|---|---|---|
| As reported by Wafeq | ASP by 31 July 2026 | Not stated | ASP by 31 March 2027 |
| As reported by Hawksford | Not stated | Mandatory from January 2027 | Not stated |
| As reported by ClearTax | Not stated | Not stated | All VAT-registered by July 2027 |
| Official MoF/FTA text | [Date per Ministerial Decision No. 244 of 2025] | [Date per Ministerial Decision No. 244 of 2025] | [Date per Ministerial Decision No. 244 of 2025] |

Most of the confusion comes from mixing two dates. The ASP appointment deadline is when your provider contract must be in place. The go-live date is when you must issue and transmit e-invoices through that provider. Your ASP deadline comes first.

### A three-question rule to find your deadline

1. Are you VAT-registered and outside the exclusion list? If not, the mandate may not apply. Confirm with your adviser.
2. Is your revenue at or above AED 50 million? If yes, the first-phase ASP and go-live dates apply to you.
3. Have you appointed an ASP? If not, your nearest exposure is the ASP deadline, not go-live.

[Image: UAE e-invoicing timeline showing the 1 July 2026 voluntary start and mandatory phases for businesses above AED 50 million]

## Is the AED 5,000 monthly cap per violation or in total?

Sources differ. Reported wording points to a separate AED 5,000 monthly cap for invoices and for credit notes, which means penalties can stack. Until the FTA clarifies, budget on the higher per-category reading and check the clause in the Ministry of Finance's published decision.

| Reading | How the cap works | Worst month, all three breaches |
|---|---|---|
| Per-category (stacking) | AED 5,000 cap for invoices, a separate AED 5,000 for credit notes, plus the system fine | AED 15,000 |
| Overall cap | One AED 5,000 ceiling across all penalties in the month | AED 5,000 |

Commentary describes the document fine as [capped at AED 5,000 per month for each](https://www.genzone.com/uae-e-invoicing-2026-guide/) category, which supports the per-category reading. Read the clause yourself in the [MoF decision](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Cabinet-Decision-Violations-and-Penalties-eInvoicing-final-version-en-8.12.25.pdf) and confirm with your tax adviser.

### How the penalties can stack in a single month

Take a business with no ASP that is also late on 60 invoices and 55 credit notes. Under the per-category reading, it faces AED 5,000 for the system and AED 5,000 for invoices. It then faces another AED 5,000 for credit notes. That is AED 15,000 for one month.

## How much could non-compliance cost? Worked penalty examples

A business with no ASP and regular late invoices faces up to AED 10,000 a month, or AED 60,000 over six months. The figures below use only the [AED 5,000 monthly fine](https://covoro.ai/uae/fta-announces-penalties-for-non-compliance-with-uae-e-invoicing/) and the [AED 100 per-document fine capped at AED 5,000](https://www.genzone.com/uae-e-invoicing-2026-guide/). Both [recur for each month or part of a month](https://kaidolab.com/blog/uae-e-invoicing-asp-deadline-2026/).

### The exposure formula

> Monthly exposure = AED 5,000 (no system or ASP) + min(late invoices × 100, 5,000) + min(late credit notes × 100, 5,000). All figures in AED per month, per-category reading.

### Three scenarios, three totals

**UAE e-invoicing penalty exposure calculator: three worked scenarios**

| Scenario | Duration (months) | Violation(s) | Monthly fine (AED) | Total: per-category cap reading (AED) | Total: overall cap reading (AED) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: enterprise above AED 50m | 6 | No ASP appointed, plus 80 late invoices a month (AED 8,000 capped to AED 5,000) | 10,000 | 60,000 | 30,000 |
| B: system live, process gaps | 3 | 30 late invoices (AED 3,000) and 10 late credit notes (AED 1,000) a month | 4,000 | 12,000 | 12,000 |
| C: no system at all | 12 | No system or ASP | 5,000 | 60,000 before invoice-level fines | 60,000 |

Scenario B is identical under both readings because its monthly total stays below AED 5,000. In Scenario C, untransmitted invoices could add up to AED 60,000 more under the per-category reading. The MoF text governs these figures, so take advice before reporting them.

### Costs that do not appear on the penalty notice

Customers who cannot process a non-compliant electronic invoice may hold payment, which affects working capital. Input VAT recovery may be questioned if invoice evidence is incomplete. Remediation also consumes finance and IT time during close. For the wider analysis, see [the full cost of e-invoicing non-compliance and mitigation](https://techand.ai/insights/the-cost-of-non-compliance-uae-e-invoicing-penalties-mitigation-costs).

## What counts as a system failure, and what if your ASP goes down?

A system failure is a technical fault in your own system or your ASP's that stops you issuing or transmitting e-invoices. You must notify the FTA within [Notification window per MoF decision]. Failing to notify carries a fine of [Amount per MoF decision]. Use the exact wording in the [MoF decision](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Cabinet-Decision-Violations-and-Penalties-eInvoicing-final-version-en-8.12.25.pdf).

An ASP outage does not remove your obligation. You still notify the FTA and keep evidence. If you assume the provider will report the outage, the notification fine falls on you.

### System-failure incident checklist

1. Detect and timestamp the failure, noting whether it sits in the ERP or the ASP.
2. Raise a ticket with your ASP and record the reference.
3. Notify the Federal Tax Authority within the required window and record the channel used.
4. Keep records of affected invoices, correspondence and screenshots.
5. Re-transmit the backlog once the system failure is resolved, then reconcile.

## Who is liable: the issuer, the recipient or the ASP?

The business is liable, not the ASP. UAE e-invoicing uses the DCTCE [five-corner model](https://qeemahcloud.com/en/blog/uae-e-invoicing-deadlines-2026/?srsltid=AU7gw4WNyQVaepjxnAO0IBhnccG4lwbSJEKQue8sg3o-iwSYmvpmKNG9) on Peppol and PINT AE. Data flows from the supplier to the supplier's ASP, then to the buyer's ASP and the buyer. The FTA is the fifth corner and receives the invoice data.

Issuers must issue and transmit invoices and each electronic credit note in the structured format on time. A PDF does not count. Issuers must also notify the FTA of system failures.

Recipients need an ASP and the ability to receive e-invoices. They must also notify the issuer of failures where the decision requires it. See [what the FTA requires under UAE e-invoicing](https://techand.ai/e-invoicing-uae-fta/) for the full obligations.

Your ASP is a service provider, so write SLAs, uptime targets and incident-reporting duties into the contract.

## How do e-invoicing fines relate to VAT penalties, and can you appeal?

They are separate schedules and can apply together. You can request reconsideration.

### Late VAT payment vs e-invoicing fines

E-invoicing fines sit in Cabinet Decision No. 106 of 2025. General VAT penalties, including late payment, sit under Cabinet Decision No. 40 of 2017 as amended. A late electronic invoice can therefore attract an e-invoicing fine and, separately, a VAT penalty. Check current late-payment rates on the Federal Tax Authority's penalty schedule rather than relying on secondary summaries.

### Requesting reconsideration from the FTA

Federal Decree-Law No. 28 of 2022 lets you request reconsideration from the FTA, followed by objection routes. Time limits are [Time limit per Federal Decree-Law No. 28 of 2022]. Your incident logs and ASP correspondence are your evidence, so keep them from day one.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q1: Is e-invoicing mandatory in the UAE?
A1: Yes, for VAT-registered businesses in scope, on a phased timetable. Voluntary adoption opens from 1 July 2026, and large businesses at or above the AED 50 million threshold move first. Check the Ministerial Decisions and FTA guidance for your exact deadline, because published secondary sources quote different dates. Our [complete guide to e-invoicing in the UAE](https://techand.ai/e-invoicing-in-uae/) covers scope.

Q2: What is the penalty for not issuing an e-invoice?
A2: Failing to issue and transmit an electronic invoice on time carries a penalty of AED 100 per invoice, capped at AED 5,000 per month ([source](https://www.genzone.com/uae-e-invoicing-2026-guide/)). If you have not implemented the system or appointed an ASP at all, a separate AED 5,000 monthly penalty can apply as well.

Q3: Who is exempted from e-invoicing?
A3: The Ministerial Decisions list excluded transactions and entities. The list is [Exclusions per Ministerial Decision No. 243 of 2025]. Being VAT-registered does not by itself mean you are in scope for every transaction. Check the official exclusion list against your revenue streams and confirm borderline cases with your tax adviser before your phase begins.

Q4: What is the penalty for late payment of VAT in the UAE?
A4: Late VAT payment penalties fall under Cabinet Decision No. 40 of 2017 as amended, not the e-invoicing decision. Rates have changed over time, so take the current figures from the Federal Tax Authority's published penalty schedule. Both penalty regimes can apply to the same business in the same period.

Q5: Are there penalties during the voluntary phase?
A5: No. Cabinet Decision No. 106 of 2025 states that its provisions do not apply to businesses that issue, transmit or exchange e-invoices voluntarily. This makes the voluntary window the safest time to test your ERP and ASP connection before your mandatory date.

Q6: What is the AED 1,000 daily penalty for?
A6: Secondary commentary links a daily figure of AED 1,000 to notification failures, such as not reporting a system failure to the FTA. We have not published it in our table because the amount must be confirmed against the MoF decision. Check the exact clause before budgeting for it.

Q7: Do e-invoicing penalties apply to credit notes?
A7: Yes. Each electronic credit note not issued and transmitted on time costs AED 100, capped at AED 5,000 per month ([source](https://www.genzone.com/uae-e-invoicing-2026-guide/)). Reported wording suggests this cap sits separately from the invoice cap. Late credit notes could therefore add to invoice penalties in the same month.

Q8: Where can I download the UAE e-invoicing penalties PDF?
A8: The official text is the Ministry of Finance's [Cabinet Decision on e-invoicing violations and penalties](https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Cabinet-Decision-Violations-and-Penalties-eInvoicing-final-version-en-8.12.25.pdf).
